eval.title: Malibu Boats Stock Analysis

call.headline_quote: no point in making the valuation of something that we can not know what happens to margin and revenues if hits the fan

what_is_priced_in.quote: why such a low p ratio because 2022 was great and the market expects that sales will go down especially as interest rates go up

reasons.claim: Boat demand is deeply cyclical and can collapse 50-70% in a recession, making forward margins and revenue unpredictable.
reasons.quote: this is minus what is this 50 70 60 70 that is the destruction that happens in a recession

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: peak-to-trough decline

reasons.claim: Rising consumer loan rates make boats, a discretionary luxury purchase, much more expensive and could crush demand.
reasons.quote: now we are already 6.57 which means that boats are much more expensive especially if you buy them on a loan

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: consumer loan rate

reasons.claim: A potential 200 million legal liability could seriously hurt the company especially if it hits during a low-earnings period of the cycle.
reasons.quote: this is 140 million potential maximum liability plus interest so that's potential 200 million that might come for the company to be paid

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: potential maximum liability

reasons.claim: The stock's low P/E of 6-10 reflects peak cyclical earnings, and buying when it looks ugly (in the trough) has historically doubled money.
reasons.quote: if they make now 100 million in cash flow p ratio is 10 if things turns out they'll still hopefully make 20 to 50 million

data_check.gap_note: he says 10, as-of 7.20373 (FY2022); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Growth has come from disciplined acquisitions of premium boat brands funded by internally generated cash, with debt being paid down quickly.
reasons.quote: they have really benefited from the Boom in people buying boats as they had a lot of money especially from their low interest loans and stimulus money

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: cobalt boats acquisition, pursuit boats acquisition

external_facts_used: Seeking Alpha analyst articles reviewed for trendline and key factors
Performance sport retail sales / boat industry historical cycle data (2006 peak, 2010 trough)
Competitor data from Mastercraft, Marine Products, Brunswick Corporation
Consumer loan interest rate level of 6.57%

critic.notes: He declines a formal valuation but still judges: not now, only interesting much lower (~300-500M cap) in the trough; that reads as avoid rather than too_hard. Both map to SELL. Reason 5 'disciplined' is mild embellishment.
